items.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022
items.q: I really got through it ... I got one of them by Stan Getz ... Cannonball Adderley and Coltrane ... I gravitated more towards the tenor. I still loved the alto sound. Cannon had it.

ctx.x: When you heard Cannonball followed by Coltrane, were you at the point — this is seventh grade now — can you recall a preference or distinguishing one from the other?

I didn’t have a preference, however, my ear gravitated more to the tenor, the tenor sound. And actually yeah, yeah. I really got through it — no, no they were both — I was in junior high when I was listening to both of them. Because what I did was I had the opportunity to join the Columbia Record Club. You know, ten albums for 99 cents and then they send you a new one each month and then you take it or not. But records that I bought I got “Kind of Blue” I got one of them by Stan Getz “Dear Old Stockholm,”…
Yeah. I’m a huge fan as well. And he had that tone that sort of leapt off the record.
